concerns.message: The corner approach in item 8 does not moor from 'any lateral offset'. It only works when the hull starts east of the land beside the dock with room for its drift. Heading 47 at full speed moves dx=-3 and dy=-38 per step (heading 46: dx=-7), so over the 3-tile run the ship drifts about 64 sub-units west (about 150 at heading 46). If the hull's left edge ends up in column dock.tileX-1, it hits the land beside the dock from the south. It then slides west along the island's south shore at full speed, is never grounded on both axes, and never moors. It also only works if the tiles north of the approach columns are land (row dock.tileY-1 for columns dock.tileX+1 to +2). If the shore steps back there, the ship passes the dock row and grounds one row higher. From there `dockInReach`'s hull-path check cuts the land corner, so it refuses to moor. The test's map check only covers the dock's own row.
concerns.consequence: The browser test can time out whenever sailTo stops at the dock.tileX+1 waypoint on its west side: `within: TILE` allows up to 256 sub-units of error, and the ship keeps coasting while it turns. The unit sweep 'across the tile' would still pass, because it never starts from the band that fails. That repeats the flake this item is meant to fix, in the fourth revision.

concerns.message: Item 8's sweep should start from the band sailTo actually leaves the ship in, not only one tile's width. That means start x from dock.tileX*256 to (dock.tileX+3)*256, a starting speed of 0 and sailTo's arrival speed, and the turn from the previous leg's heading. The browser test should use +2, or coast to a stop before turning (a ship can turn at speed 0), and assert the minimum safe x taken from the sweep.
concerns.consequence: Without this, the unit test proves the rule where the ship never actually starts, and the 5-repeat run becomes the only real check.

concerns.message: 'Within ±25 % of today's' handling (time to full speed, stopping distance, turning circle in pixels) needs today's values (64/4/8/2/24, 16 px) kept as a named baseline in the test. Once `shipTuning` changes, the old numbers no longer exist anywhere in the code.
concerns.consequence: A test that derives both sides from the current `shipTuning` becomes a tautology and can't catch retuning that moves outside the ±25 % band.

concerns.message: One hand-built layout has to meet many coupled constraints: the hub cut for every dock pair, density with no credit for the map edge, a neighbour floor of at least 61 path tiles (so every dock sits at least ~31 octile tiles from the hub gap), spawn slots outside the islands' bounding box, a south dock with land to the west, sea to the east and a shoal bar to sail around, and the clear out-of-sight row beside a wall.
concerns.consequence: Fitting these one at a time against `map:build`'s validators can take many iterations. That risks the two-hour stop condition, or a map that passes the validators but has no usable test geometry, which means reworking the tests.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: Write the sketch script to draw one 56 × 56 quadrant (one island with its docks, two spawn slots, obstacles, and half of each midline wall ending at the hub gap) and rotate it three times by 90° around the centre. Neighbour times, spawn-to-dock times and density then match for all four quadrants by construction, so only one quadrant needs tuning against the validators. Have the script also assert the two test geometries (the corner-dock tiles, including row dock.tileY-1 east of the dock, and the out-of-sight row with its turning side), so a layout change breaks the sketch rather than the browser tests.
structured_output.cheap_experiment: Before drawing the map, write the corner-approach sweep as a simulation unit test on a tiny synthetic map: a dock with land to the north and west, and sea to the east and south. Using the proposed tuning (maxSpeed 39, accel 3, drag 1, dockMaxSpeed about 15), start the ship 3 tiles south with start x from dock.tileX*256 to (dock.tileX+3)*256 in 16-sub-unit steps. Try headings 46 and 47, and starting states of speed 0, and speed about 20 turning in from heading 32. Record the smallest start x that still moors. This takes minutes. It settles +1 against +2, whether to coast to a stop before turning, and what safe band the browser test should assert.
